Options:

Small-C/Plus - z80 Crosscompiler   Version: 25851-895dc13665-20260909
(C) 1980-2025 Cain, Van Zandt, Hendrix, Yorston, z88dk
Usage: /home/tstih/data/retro-vault/xyz/build/toolchains/latest-20260909/nightly-source/z88dk/bin/z88dk-sccz80 [flags] [file]
   -v -verbose                  Be verbose
   -h -help                     Show this help page
   -o -output                   Set the output filename

CPU Targetting:
      -m8080                    Generate output for the i8080
      -m8085                    Generate output for the i8085
      -mvm1                     Generate output for the KR580VM1
      -mez80_z80                Generate output for the ez80 in z80 mode
      -mz80                     Generate output for the z80
      -mz80n                    Generate output for the z80n
      -mz180                    Generate output for the z180
      -mr2ka                    Generate output for the Rabbit 2000A
      -mr3k                     Generate output for the Rabbit 3000
      -mr4k                     Generate output for the Rabbit 4000
      -mr6k                     Generate output for the Rabbit 4000
      -mgbz80                   Generate output for the Gameboy CPU
      -mkc160                   Generate output for the KC160

Code generation options
      -unsigned                 Make all types unsigned
      --disable-builtins        Disable builtin functions
      --reserve-regs-iy         (ignored) sdcc/80cc register-reservation flag
      --reserve-regs-ix         (ignored) sdcc/80cc register-reservation flag
      -params-offset            =<num> Base offset for the function parameters (default: 2)
      -doublestr                Store FP constants as strings
      -math-z88                 (deprecated) Make FP constants match z88
      -banked-style=regular     Use regular banked calling style
      -banked-style=ti          Use ticalc banked calling style
      -fp-exponent-bias         =<num> FP exponent bias (default: 128)
      -fp-mantissa-size         =<num> FP mantissa size (default: 5 bytes)
      -fp-mode=z80              Use 48 bit doubles
      -fp-mode=ieee             Use 32 bit IEEE doubles
      -fp-mode=mbf32            Use 32 bit Microsoft Binary format
      -fp-mode=mbf40            Use 40 bit Microsoft binary format
      -fp-mode=mbf64            Use 64 bit Microsoft binary format
      -fp-mode=z88              Use 40 bit z88 doubles
      -fp-mode=am9511           Use 32 bit AM9511 doubles
      -noaltreg                 Try not to use the alternative register set
      -standard-escape-chars    Use standard mappings for \r and \n
      -set-r2l-by-default       Use r->l calling convention by default
      --constseg                =<name> Set the const section name
      --codeseg                 =<name> Set the code section name
      --bssseg                  =<name> Set the bss section name
      --dataseg                 =<name> Set the data section name
      --initseg                 =<name> Set the initialisation section name
      -gcline                   Generate C_LINE directives
      --opt-code-speed          Optimise for speed not size

Framepointer configuration (for debugging):
      -frameix                  Use ix as the frame pointer
      -frameiy                  Use iy as the frame pointer
      -zcc-opt                  Location for zcc_opt.def

Error/warning handling:
      -stop-on-error            Stop on any error
      --old-diagnostic-format   Use old style diagnostic messages
      -W                        <type> Enable a class of warnings

Debugging options
      -debug-sect               Create adb/cdb debug section
      -debug-defc               Create adb/cdb debug defc
      -cc                       Intersperse the assembler output with the source C code
      -intlog                   =<val> Enable some extra logging
      -ext                      =<ext> Set the file extension for the generated output
      -D                        Define a preprocessor directive
      -U                        Undefine a preprocessor directive

Assignments can either be = or as next argument
versions.nightly_80cc:
Options:

80cc - z80 family Crosscompiler   Version: 25851-895dc13665-20260909
(C) 1980-2026 Cain, Van Zandt, Hendrix, Yorston, z88dk
Usage: /home/tstih/data/retro-vault/xyz/build/toolchains/latest-20260909/nightly-source/z88dk/bin/z88dk-80cc [flags] [file]
   -v -verbose                  Be verbose
   -h -help                     Show this help page
   -o -output                   Set the output filename

CPU Targetting:
      -m8080                    Generate output for the i8080
      -m8085                    Generate output for the i8085
      -mez80_z80                Generate output for the ez80 in z80 mode
      -mz80                     Generate output for the z80
      -mz80n                    Generate output for the z80n
      -mz180                    Generate output for the z180
      -mr2ka                    Generate output for the Rabbit 2000A
      -mr3k                     Generate output for the Rabbit 3000
      -mr4k                     Generate output for the Rabbit 4000
      -mr6k                     Generate output for the Rabbit 4000
      -mgbz80                   Generate output for the Gameboy CPU
      -mkc160                   Generate output for the KC160
      -mvm1                     Generate output for the KR580VM1

Code generation options
      -unsigned                 Make all types unsigned
      --disable-builtins        Disable builtin functions
      -params-offset            =<num> Base offset for the function parameters (default: 2)
      -math-z88                 (deprecated) Make FP constants match z88
      -banked-style=regular     Use regular banked calling style
      -banked-style=ti          Use ticalc banked calling style
      -fp-exponent-bias         =<num> FP exponent bias (default: 128)
      -fp-mantissa-size         =<num> FP mantissa size (default: 5 bytes)
      -fp-mode=z80              Use 48 bit doubles
      -fp-mode=ieee             Use 32 bit IEEE doubles
      -fp-mode=mbf32            Use 32 bit Microsoft Binary format
      -fp-mode=mbf40            Use 40 bit Microsoft binary format
      -fp-mode=mbf64            Use 64 bit Microsoft binary format
      -fp-mode=z88              Use 40 bit z88 doubles
      -fp-mode=am9511           Use 32 bit AM9511 doubles
      -standard-escape-chars    Use standard mappings for \r and \n (inert — escapes are always standard)
      -set-r2l-by-default       Use r->l calling convention by default
      --constseg                =<name> Set the const section name
      --codeseg                 =<name> Set the code section name
      --bssseg                  =<name> Set the bss section name
      --dataseg                 =<name> Set the data section name
      --initseg                 =<name> Set the initialisation section name
      -gcline                   Generate C_LINE directives
      --opt-disable             =<list> Disable named optimiser passes (comma-separated). AST passes: all, fold, prop, simplify, typecheck, compoundify, strength-reduce, cse, cse-synth, licm, dse, dead-code, thread-jumps, demote-poststep, loop-reverse. IR/lowering gates by name, e.g. lra, bc-pack, bc-evict, de-home, ivsr, lftr, addr-cse, label-elide, lazy-spill, remat, idx2, idx3, gpderef, declean (see opt_disabled call sites). pattern:<name> disables one IR pattern-matcher entry. `all` disables every optimisation. Useful for bisecting miscompiles.
      --opt-code-speed          (inert) Accepted for --math16 alias / sccz80-family CLI compatibility; no effect in the IR back end
      --ast-print               (experimental) Build the AST per function, print it to stderr, and skip code generation
      --ast-print-types         (experimental) Decorate the AST print with type/qualifier/attribute info; implies --ast-print

Frame pointer / index-register reservation:
      -fframe-pointer           Use IX as a frame pointer (address locals via ix+d)
      -fomit-frame-pointer      Omit the frame pointer; address locals via sp (default)
      --reserve-regs-iy         Reserve IY: never use it for residency (leaves at most one index register)
      --reserve-regs-ix         Reserve IX (sp-mode): do not use it as the spare index register
      --reg-index-invariant     Hold a loop-invariant in the spare index register (IX in sp-mode, IY in fp-mode)
      --no-reg-index-invariant  Disable the spare-index-register loop-invariant resident
      --reg-iy-half             (experimental) Hold a second loop-carried word in IY via index-half ops (ld iyl,c / sub iyl); sp-mode, z80/z80n only — undocumented opcodes, IY is callee-saved
      --no-reg-iy-half          Disable the index-half IY residency
      --exx                     (experimental) Hold a loop-invariant in the exx/alt register set (sp-mode, z80/z80n)
      --no-exx                  Disable exx/alt register-set residency
      --byte-resident           Keep a hot loop-carried char accumulator in a byte register
      --no-byte-resident        Disable byte-register residency for char accumulators
      --word-resident           Keep a hot loop-carried int accumulator in the DE register pair
      --no-word-resident        Disable word-register residency for int accumulators
      -zcc-opt                  Location for zcc_opt.def

Error/warning handling:
      -stop-on-error            Stop on any error
      --old-diagnostic-format   Use old style diagnostic messages
      -W                        <type> Enable a class of warnings

Debugging options
      -debug-defc               Create sdcc-compatible cdb debug info (defc __CDBINFO__)
      -cc                       Intersperse the assembler output with the source C code
      -intlog                   =<val> Enable some extra logging
      -ext                      =<ext> Set the file extension for the generated output
      -D                        Define a preprocessor directive
      -U                        Undefine a preprocessor directive
      -I                        Add an include path (forwarded to the preprocessor)
      --c1mode                  Input is already preprocessed; skip the internal ucpp invocation
      --lex-only                Dump token stream from the internal tokeniser to stdout and exit (Phase L2)
      --cpp                     =<path> Override the preprocessor binary (default z88dk-ucpp)

Assignments can either be = or as next argument
